content:
Latest update, 7:37 PM ET: Apple says all issues have been resolved except for Apple TV.

Apple is now reporting problems with Apple TV and subscription purchases, with some users also affected by other services. Details below.

Apple is now listing 8 ongoing issues.

Apple's System Status page currently lists Apple TV, the App Store, Apple Fitness+, Apple Music, Apple Music Subscriptions, Mac App Store, and subscription purchases as experiencing outages or other ongoing issues.

According to Apple, most of the issues began at 4:22 PM ET. The company has listed the App Store, Apple Music, and Mac App Store as undergoing "routine maintenance, which is not expected to impact users," while the Apple TV outage began at 4:43 PM ET, which Apple said "may be temporarily unavailable due to scheduled maintenance."

During our testing, the Apple TV interface failed to load on iOS, but content was still loading and playing normally on other devices.

The outages came shortly after multiple apps — including TestFlight, the App Store, and Fitness+ — began replacing normal interface text with internal localization strings. It's unclear at this point whether that's related to Apple's broader issues.

Reports on Downdetector further confirm that Apple TV is affected, although the number of reports appears to have peaked and begun declining, suggesting the outage may be tapering off.

We'll continue to monitor the situation closely and update this article as we learn more or as Apple marks issues as resolved.

Are you affected? Let us know in the comments.

Notable Amazon products

  • Apple Watch Series 12
  • Apple Watch Ultra 4
  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods 5
  • AirTag (2nd generation) — 4-pack
  • MacBook Neo
  • Logitech MX Master 4
